validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: confirmed real and correctly classified. offshore-technology.com (independent, non-GEM, verified live) states gas from the Bahr Essalam field 'is transported via a 36in-diameter pipeline to the onshore Mellitah plant for final treatment' -- this is the exact pipeline recorded as P1855 (36in, Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission). Same source separately states 'Condensate travels through a separate 10-inch diameter pipeline to Mellitah' -- confirming the field runs TWO parallel lines to Mellitah, not one. DUPLICATE CHECK vs roster: P6713 in the roster carries the identical name 'Bahr Assalam–Mellitah Gas Pipeline' with dia=10, cap=465166.0, len=109.0 -- same route, same 109km length, but a DIFFERENT diameter (10in vs 36in). Cross-checked against the sheet's own already-cited OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin (ASB2013 Table 4.10, 2012 data, and ASB2017 Table 9.9, 2016 data -- both engaged as starting-point sources per the sheet's wiki_citations, manually extracted via pdftotext since raw-HTTP substring matching cannot read compressed PDF streams -- a documented content false-negative class, not a live-source problem): both tables list 'Bahr Assalam/Mellitah' (also rendered 'Bahr es Salam/Mellitah (2)') as TWO separate pipelines sharing the route, one 36in and one 10in, each ~68-68.2 miles long. This matches offshore-technology's explicit statement that the 10in line carries condensate (a distinct commodity/purpose) while the 36in line (this row, P1855) carries sales gas. CONCLUSION: P1855 and P6713 are NOT duplicates -- they are two genuinely separate, correctly-split parallel pipelines (gas vs condensate). Confirmed P1855 is real, correctly classified as a gas transmission trunk line. One live-verifiable source (offshore-technology.com) plus the sheet's own pre-cited OPEC tables (manually confirmed, not freshly re-verifiable via automated tool at time of audit due to a transient OPEC.org Cloudflare block hit during this session) corroborate the split.

validity.researcher_notes: SPEC -- Capacity disagreement. GEM records Capacity=28.00 bcm/y for this 36in gas line. Two independent lines of evidence disagree, both roughly 2.5x lower: (1) offshore-technology.com (live-verified) states the field 'currently produces 1,100 million standard cubic feet of gas per day' of sales gas (post-2018 Phase II expansion, up from ~600-700 MMscfd for Phase I) -- 1,100 MMscfd converts to ~11.4 bcm/y, and this sales-gas volume is exactly what the 36in pipeline (this row) carries to Mellitah, since the source separately confirms condensate goes via the other (10in) line. (2) The sheet's own pre-cited OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2013 (Table 4.10, 2012 data) lists the 36in Bahr Assalam/Mellitah line's capacity as 9,199,943 (in units of 1,000 scm/yr per the table header) = ~9.2 bcm/yr nameplate -- manually confirmed via pdftotext extraction of the sheet's already-cited source (could not get a fresh automated url_verifier pass on this specific PDF during this session: requests against it began returning the OPEC.org Cloudflare landing page rather than the PDF bytes partway through the session, and even when the real PDF is fetched, raw substring matching against compressed PDF streams is a known false-negative pattern -- so this OPEC figure is reported here as manually-reviewed context from the sheet's own cited source, not as a freshly re-verified citation). Both figures (9.2 bcm/y 2012 nameplate; ~11.4 bcm/y 2026 actual throughput after the 2018 capacity expansion) are internally consistent with each other and with the Phase II expansion timeline, and both are far below GEM's recorded 28.00 bcm/y. Recommend the sheet's Capacity value be corrected downward or re-sourced -- not confirmed as-is.
